status: Draft. Who does each step, how, and how long are a strawman from general practice, not yet reviewed by an SME.

template.label: Template
template.note: Fixed wording from this template; the same on every block until an SME edits it.

funding.label: Funding agent
funding.note: FundingAgent's approved funding matches for this recommendation.

zoning.label: Zoning lookup
zoning.note: The zones fronting the block from the county zoning map, checked against the Zoning Ordinance's use tables (§27-5101). A lookup, not a model: every finding cites its source.

policy.label: Policy agent
policy.note: PolicyAgent (supporting or blocking plans and codes) is not built yet, so the SME supplies this.
policy.why: A grant or approval is stronger when an adopted plan already calls for the change. The area plan for this block is the 2022 Bowie-Mitchellville and Vicinity Master Plan, which the 2024 rezoning implements.
policy.ask: Which adopted plan or policy supports {thing} on {street}, and where (chapter, strategy or page)?

ref.label: 2022 Approved Bowie-Mitchellville and Vicinity Master Plan (M-NCPPC)

parcel.label: Parcel lookup
parcel.note: County parcel records (owner and site) are not connected yet, so the SME supplies this.
parcel.why: Who owns the land decides who acts: the City can only start work on land it controls, and private owners have to agree to anything on theirs.
parcel.ask: Who owns the parcels along {street} that this would touch: the City, M-NCPPC, another public agency, or private owners?

ref.label: Maryland SDAT real property records (owner of record per parcel)

road_owner.label: Road-owner lookup
road_owner.note: Whether the road is State (MD SHA), County or City is not looked up yet, so the SME supplies this.
road_owner.why: The road owner approves and permits anything in the right-of-way. On a state route that is MD SHA, which adds its own studies and access permits.
road_owner.ask: Who owns {street}: the State (MD SHA), Prince George's County or the City of Bowie?

ref.label: Road ownership: MD SHA, Prince George's County DPW&T or City of Bowie records

program_terms.label: Program-terms lookup
program_terms.note: The funding program's post-award rules are not extracted yet, so the SME supplies this.
program_terms.why: An award usually comes with conditions, such as matching funds, design approval or construction deadlines, and reporting, which set the timing of the later steps.
program_terms.ask: What does the chosen funding program require after award (match, deadlines for design and construction, reporting)?

ref.label: The chosen program's notice of funding or award agreement

pathways.name: Building and façade
pathways.branch: Is the condition a code violation the City can enforce, or an improvement beyond code that needs an incentive?

steps.title: Identify the property owners on the block
steps.how: Pull the owner and mailing address of each parcel fronting the block from the state property records (SDAT) or the county's parcel map.

steps.title: Decide the path: code violation or voluntary improvement
steps.how: Compare each building's condition with the property maintenance code: what the code requires can be enforced; anything beyond it needs an owner who wants to do it.

steps.title: Inspect and issue a notice of violation; owner corrects
steps.how: Code enforcement inspects, sends the owner a notice with a deadline to correct, then re-inspects. Cases that stay open move to a citation.

steps.title: Find incentives: façade grant or loan, storefront program
steps.how: The funding agent matches façade grants, loans and storefront programs to this recommendation. Staff keep the ones worth offering to owners.

steps.title: Meet the owners; each decides whether to take part
steps.how: Staff contact each owner with the incentives on offer and the owner's share of the cost. Each owner decides whether to take part.

steps.title: Apply for the chosen program (the City or the owner, per program rules)
steps.how: The owner (or the City, if the program requires it) applies with photos, the planned work and a contractor's quote.

steps.title: Design review of the façade change, if design rules apply
steps.how: If the block is under design standards, staff or the review board check materials, signs and colours before any permit.

steps.title: Building or sign permit
steps.how: The owner's contractor files drawings for a building or sign permit; the permitting office reviews and issues it.

steps.title: Work done and inspected; incentive paid on completion
steps.how: The owner's contractor does the work. The City inspects it and pays the incentive against receipts once it is complete.

pathways.name: Land use and development
pathways.branch: Is the use allowed by right, by special exception, or not at all without rezoning? Reductions mostly happen when a site redevelops.

steps.title: Look up the zone of each parcel on the block
steps.how: The zoning lookup reads the zones fronting the block from the county zoning map.

steps.title: Check whether the use is allowed: by right, special exception, or not allowed
steps.how: The lookup checks this use against the Zoning Ordinance use tables (§27-5101) for each zone: by right, special exception, or prohibited.

steps.title: Check what the area master plan says for the site
steps.how: Staff read the 2022 Bowie-Mitchellville and Vicinity Master Plan for the site's planned land use and any strategy that calls for this use.

steps.title: If not allowed by right: special exception hearing, or rezoning / text amendment
steps.how: The applicant files for a special exception, heard by the Zoning Hearing Examiner, or asks the District Council to rezone or amend the text. Both need public notice and a hearing.
steps.owner: Zoning Hearing Examiner or District Council (confirm)

steps.title: Test the market: a willing owner or developer, and demand
steps.how: Economic development staff look for a willing owner or developer and check demand: comparable projects, rents, and how well the site fits.

steps.title: Line up incentives to close any financing gap (tax credits, state programs)
steps.how: The funding agent matches tax credits and state programs to this recommendation; staff work out which close the gap.

steps.title: Developer applies for site plan approval
steps.how: The developer submits a detailed site plan. Planning Board (M-NCPPC) staff review it and the Board decides at a hearing.

steps.title: Permits: building and stormwater, plus a state access permit on state routes
steps.how: Building and stormwater permits from the county; on a state route, an access permit from MD SHA for driveways and frontage work.

steps.title: Construction
steps.how: The developer builds, with county inspections along the way and a use and occupancy permit at the end.

pathways.name: Parks and public space
pathways.branch: Is the site City land, county parkland (M-NCPPC) or private land? Is it construction, or programming like a farmers market?

steps.title: Pick a site and confirm who controls it
steps.how: Staff shortlist sites on or near the block and check land records for who owns each: the City, M-NCPPC, or a private owner.

steps.title: Secure the site: purchase, lease or easement
steps.how: Negotiate a purchase, lease or easement with the owner. Council approves any purchase.

steps.title: Check zoning allows park use on the parcel
steps.how: The zoning lookup checks that the parcel's zone allows a park or this use.

steps.title: Collect policy to cite: parks plan, master plan, health goals
steps.how: Gather the parks plan, master plan and health goals that call for this, with page numbers, to cite in grant applications.

steps.title: Community input on the concept
steps.how: Public meetings and a survey on what the space should hold. The results shape the concept.

steps.title: Concept design and cost estimate
steps.how: Staff or a consultant draw a concept plan and cost estimate, detailed enough to apply for grants.

steps.title: Apply for state or federal parks grants
steps.how: Staff apply to the programs the funding agent matched, using the concept, the cost estimate and the policy citations.

steps.title: If awarded: council accepts the grant; notify the planning committee
steps.how: Council votes to accept the grant and any local match, and the planning committee is told.

steps.title: Final design approval, within the program's deadline
steps.how: Finish the design and get the funding agency's sign-off before the program's deadline.

steps.title: Permits: site, grading, stormwater
steps.how: Site, grading and stormwater permits from the county.

steps.title: Bid and award the construction contract
steps.how: City procurement puts the work out to bid and council awards the contract.

steps.title: Build, then grant close-out and a maintenance plan
steps.how: The contractor builds it. The City closes out the grant and sets a maintenance plan and budget.

pathways.name: Traffic control and crossings
pathways.branch: Is the road state (MD SHA), county or City? Signs and markings move fast; signals need a warrant study and take much longer.

steps.title: Confirm who owns the road
steps.how: Check whether the road is a City street, a county road or a state route (MD SHA), from the road ownership maps.

steps.title: Request an engineering study: a crossing study, or a warrant analysis for signals and stop signs
steps.how: Ask the road owner for a crossing study, or a warrant analysis under the MUTCD for a signal or stop sign: counts, speeds and crash history.

steps.title: Road owner approves the treatment
steps.how: The road owner reviews the study and approves a treatment, or says why not.

steps.title: Find funding: maintenance budget for markings, grants for signals
steps.how: The funding agent matches safety and transportation grants. Markings usually come out of the road owner's maintenance budget.

steps.title: Agreement or permit, if the City pays for or builds on a road it doesn't own
steps.how: If the City pays for or builds on a county or state road, sign an agreement or get a permit from the road owner.

steps.title: Design to the Maryland MUTCD
steps.how: Signs, markings or signal plans are designed to the Maryland MUTCD.

steps.title: Install
steps.how: The road owner's crews or a contractor install it.
steps.time: Weeks for markings; 3–6 mo for signals

steps.title: Agree who maintains it
steps.how: Put in writing who maintains the signs, markings or signal, and who pays.

pathways.name: Streetscape and sidewalks
pathways.branch: Who owns the road? Is the item capital work, a furnishing, a service an operator runs (bus stops, bike share), or a business permit (outdoor dining)?

steps.title: Confirm the road owner and the space available in the right-of-way
steps.how: Check who owns the road and measure the space in the right-of-way for sidewalks, trees, lights or furnishings.

steps.title: Collect policy to cite: complete streets, bike and pedestrian plans
steps.how: Gather the complete streets, bike and pedestrian plans that call for this, with page numbers, to cite in applications.

steps.title: Get into a capital budget, or a small-works budget for furnishings
steps.how: Ask for the project in the City's capital improvement program, or a small-works line for furnishings such as benches.

steps.title: Apply for transportation or streetscape grants
steps.how: Staff apply to the transportation and streetscape programs the funding agent matched.

steps.title: If awarded: council accepts; federal money adds environmental review
steps.how: Council accepts the grant. Federal money adds an environmental review, run with MD SHA.
steps.owner: City Council; MD SHA for federal aid

steps.title: Design, utility coordination and ADA compliance
steps.how: The City engineer or a consultant designs it, coordinates with utilities, and checks ADA compliance.

steps.title: Permits: right-of-way permit; street trees may need a state roadside tree permit
steps.how: A right-of-way permit from the road owner. Street trees may also need a state roadside tree permit.

steps.title: Bid and build
steps.how: The City bids the work and a contractor builds it.

steps.title: Agree who maintains benches, trees and lights
steps.how: Put in writing who maintains the benches, trees and lights, and who pays.

pathways.name: Road and curb changes
pathways.branch: Who owns the road? Lane reductions need traffic analysis and public engagement; driveway reductions usually wait for redevelopment.

steps.title: Confirm who owns the road
steps.how: Check whether the road is a City street, a county road or a state route (MD SHA), from the road ownership maps.

steps.title: Traffic and parking study: volumes for lane cuts; width and sight lines for parking
steps.how: The road owner studies traffic volumes for a lane reduction, or width and sight lines for parking.

steps.title: Collect policy to cite: complete streets, road diet guidance
steps.how: Gather the complete streets and road diet guidance that supports this, to cite to the road owner and the public.

steps.title: Public engagement with businesses and residents
steps.how: Meetings with the businesses and residents on the block about what changes and why.

steps.title: Road owner approves
steps.how: The road owner approves the change, using the study and what the public said.

steps.title: Time it with scheduled resurfacing, or fund it separately
steps.how: Fold the change into the next scheduled resurfacing, which costs least, or fund it on its own.

steps.title: Striping and signing plan
steps.how: An engineer draws the striping and signing plan.

steps.title: Restripe and sign
steps.how: The road owner's crews restripe and sign the road.

steps.title: Driveways: consolidate with owners, usually at redevelopment
steps.how: Driveways are consolidated with the owners, usually when a site redevelops. See the land use and development playbook.
